- When sentiment is consistently negative (last 3–5 days), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior 30d mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 3–7 days; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak.
- If sentiment turns positive after a downtrend, model frequently underreacts; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% per sentiment shift.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >10% above recent 18d average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30d horizon, model often overweights short-term volatility; smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ values before projecting.
- If sentiment is negative and price is rising, model may misread sentiment; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per negative sentiment unit.
